bull.b: Sustained, very large revenue growth alongside sharply higher adjusted EBITDA indicates scalable demand and improving operating leverage across segments. This durable margin expansion (adjusted) supports reinvestment capacity and validates commercial traction even while GAAP losses persist.

Rapid subscriber adds and a large, expanding satellite fleet create structural network effects and unit-cost declines as deployment scales. Enterprise and government growth channel diversification improves revenue durability and underpins longer-term recurring cash flows from connectivity services.

Very large cash reserves, fresh IPO proceeds and bond issuance materially reduce short-term funding risk and enable multi-year investment programs. This liquidity gives management flexibility to fund high CapEx, scale Starlink and compute builds, and absorb execution timing without immediate refinancing pressure.

bear.b: Sustained, large-scale CapEx programs materially widen the gap between operating cash flow and free cash flow, increasing funding sensitivity. If returns on these investments lag expectations, persistent negative FCF will pressure liquidity over multiple quarters despite current cash buffers.

A swing to deeply negative net margins despite top-line growth signals elevated operating leverage risk from R&D and infrastructure spend. Structural profitability recovery depends on converting adjusted EBITDA into sustained GAAP profits once heavy investment phases conclude and cost discipline scales.

Dependence on a single GPU supplier and tight memory markets can bottleneck compute expansion, raise costs, and delay revenue from AI services. Structural supply concentration increases execution risk for the compute growth thesis and can compress margins if alternative sourcing is limited.
